title: NRPyLaTeX metric-assignment directives
objective: Add two `% mechanics assign` directives that let a LaTeX source declare the current and reference metrics directly. Auto-compute Christoffel symbols whenever the metric is assigned.

plan_assets.asset_description: B2.4 directive syntax: `% mechanics assign gDD --metric_current` and `% mechanics assign GDD --metric_reference`.

scope: Extend the `% mechanics` directive parser introduced in §A3 to handle the new `assign` command.
The directive body takes a tensor symbol name and an option: `--metric_current` or `--metric_reference`.
On parse, record the assignment in the context dict; downstream (lowering or compile step) reads it and populates the corresponding metric on `ConfigurationIR`.
Auto-generate the Christoffel symbols and cache them on the IR.
implementation_steps: Add an `assign` handler to `mechdsl.frontend.directives` alongside the existing seven handlers.
Validate that the metric assignment points at a tensor the NRPyLaTeX side can resolve (this may be a stub for now; Plan B frontend integration is a separate workstream).
Add parser tests: parse the MVP curvilinear example and verify the assignment appears in the context dict.
Add an end-to-end test that wires a cylindrical metric through build_context to ElementIR.
acceptance_criteria: `parse('% mechanics assign gDD --metric_current\n...')` round-trips without raising.
The context dict contains the metric assignment entries.
Cylindrical metric example propagates from parser to ElementIR.
risks: Full NRPyLaTeX integration for user-defined equations is a separate workstream. Mitigation: accept the directive syntactically and stash the metric expression as a string; defer full evaluation to a follow-up task.
completion_notes: All 3 gates passed first attempt. e2e test skipped (Plan B B2.5). 5 passed + 1 e2e skip.
